question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
For employees of the existing National Building Research Organisation, the option to opt out of employment in the new Institute must be exercised "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [621/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- That six-month window applies only to NRBO staff offered employment on commencement; declining triggers compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme [621/2025 §33(2)(c)].
- Section 20 (temporary/permanent appointment of public officers to the Institute's staff) contains no right to decline and no time limit [621/2025 §20].

Caveats: The evidence does not state any period for declining an offer outside the NRBO transfer provision; a clause on that point appears to be missing. This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-07-17), not a Bill as presented.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
The exclusion applies to years of assessment **prior to April 1, 2018** — the new section 202(2A)(a) provides that subsection (2) "shall not apply" to such deductions [013/2026 §37].

- It covers amounts already deducted under section 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act, "notwithstanding that any un-deducted balance" remains as at April 1, 2018 [013/2026 §37].
- Source bill: Inland Revenue (Amendment) — GS, published 2026-02-24 [013/2026 §1].

Caveats: This is the Gazette (GS) version; no presented-Bill text is in the evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 013/2026 §1

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A moneylender’s licence issued or renewed is valid for **one year** [645/2025 §25(c)]. A **microfinance institution** licence is instead issued for **three years** [645/2025 §32(7)], and the three-year period expressly applies to renewals [645/2025 §32(9)].

- Moneylending licence: “valid for a period of one year” [645/2025 §25(c)].
- Microfinance licence: “issued for a period of three years” [645/2025 §32(7)].
- This is the Gazette version, dated 2025-11-17 [645/2025 §25].

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
A renewal application must be submitted "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration" of the existing licence [657/2025 §6(1)].

- The application must be in the prescribed Form and accompanied by the prescribed renewal fee [657/2025 §6(1)].
- Renewal is then granted if the licensee has not breached licence terms or the Act, and continued operation will not adversely affect the public [657/2025 §6(2)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-12-12); no presented Bill version appears in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
The amendment raises the outer time limit in section 8(2)(b) from **“a period of two years” to “a period of three years”**, so the new maximum appears to be **three years** [020/2026 §9]. It also raises the shorter cap from **“shall not exceed three months” to “shall not exceed four months”** [020/2026 §9].

- The bill is the **Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment)** — GS, dated **2026-03-17** [020/2026 §1].

Caveat: the evidence quotes only the substituted phrases, not the full section 8(2)(b), so the exact interaction between the four-month cap and three-year total is not fully shown.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 020/2026 §1

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
Monthly — the substituted section 2 charges the levy "in respect of each month" on the value of telecommunication services supplied by an operator or provider [028/2026 §2].

- The levy is charged to "every person receiving any telecommunication service" at the rate in the Schedule [028/2026 §2], which is 15% for non-internet services from June 4, 2022, and 0% for internet services from September 1, 2017 [028/2026 §7].
- Diplomatic Privileges Act entities are exempt [028/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is the Gazette (GS) version of 23 April 2026, not a presented Bill; no presented version is in the evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 028/2026 §7

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Under the amended section 49(5) of the Bills of Exchange Ordinance (per the **Bills of Exchange (Amendment)** bill — GS version, published 2025-06-04), notice of dishonour may be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" [601/2025 §8].

- The electronic/facsimile route requires the notice to "sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [601/2025 §8].
- This replaces the previous subsection (5) of section 49 in its entirety [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: only the GS (pre-presentation) text is in evidence; no presented Bill version is available.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer: Under the bill, a “qualified auditor” is **(a)** an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or another institute established by law and holds a certificate to practice as an Accountant from its Council, or **(b)** a firm of accountants whose resident partners meet those membership and certificate requirements [626/2025 §11].

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
"Knowledge sharing activities" means activities designed to facilitate the exchange of ideas, skills and experiences fostering a culture of learning and collaboration [646/2025 §18].

- The term appears in §6(h), which empowers the body corporate to organize lectures, seminars, trainings and conferences "with a view to promoting the object of the body corporate" [646/2025 §6].
- This is from the bill titled **Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation)** — GS, 2025-11-20 (name matches the question) [646/2025 §1].

Caveats: only the GS version is in evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 646/2025 §1, 646/2025 §6

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Bill gives the Society power to acquire, hold and dispose of movable and immovable property: under [047/2026 §13], it may “take and hold any property, movable or immovable” acquired by “purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise,” and may “sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of” it.

- It may “purchase, rent construct, renovate and otherwise obtain lands or buildings” and deal with/dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].
- Property must be held “for the purpose of this Act” and subject to rules under section 7 [047/2026 §13].
- It may administer lawful trusts with similar objects or “any real or personal property” to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(f)].

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
The President of the Institute chairs both the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee; for other committees, where more than one Council member is appointed, the Council appoints one of them as Chairperson [656/2025 §18(2)], [656/2025 §18(3)].

- Each committee must include at least one Council member, and that member is its Chairman, except for committees (a) and (b), which the President chairs [656/2025 §18(2)].
- At committee meetings the Chairman presides; in his absence members present elect a chairperson from among themselves [656/2025 §18(5)].
- Composition, powers, duties and functions of each committee are "as specified by rules made under this Act" [656/2025 §18(4)].

Caveats: The §18(2) text as supplied is garbled/truncated around the proviso, so the chairing rule for the remaining committees rests on §18(3) plus the general rule; the detailed rules are not in the evidence. (Bill dated 2025-12-05.)

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the GS amendment dated 2025-11-28, workers hired by **pre-commencement** licensees get a three-year income-tax exemption; workers hired by licensees issued **on or after** commencement are taxable.

- Pre-commencement licensees may employ residents/non-residents paid in a “designated foreign currency, other than … Sri Lanka Rupees”; for “three years,” resident employment income is exempt and deemed a credit to a personal foreign currency account, and non-resident employment income is exempt with no Sri Lanka tax on foreign income [652/2025 §3].
- For licensees issued “on or after the date on which this section comes into operation,” employment income “shall be liable to income tax” [652/2025 §3].

Caveats: This is the Colombo Port City Economic Commission (Amendment) **GS** version; the three-year start-date wording in the evidence is garbled.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The amendment removes the reference to container operators from the long title: the words "FREIGHT FORWARDERS, NON-VESSEL OPERATING COMMON CARRIERS, AND CONTAINER OPERATORS" are replaced with "FREIGHT FORWARDERS AND NON-VESSEL OPERATING COMMON CARRIERS" [005/2026 §2].

- The bill is the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators (Amendment) Bill, dated 2026-01-20 [005/2026 §1].
- Relatedly, the definition of "container operators" in section 15 is deleted [005/2026 §4], and pending applications and existing container-operator licences are deemed to fall under the Licensing of Container Depot Operators Act, No. 2026 [005/2026 §5].
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 005/2026 §1, 005/2026 §4, 005/2026 §5

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The Bill [029/2026 §1, §2] amends the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005, mainly by widening extraterritorial application, adding new offences and raising penalties.

- Section 2A(2) is replaced so the Act applies to acts committed "wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka" directed at Sri Lanka, a Sri Lankan citizen, a government facility, or to compel the Government [029/2026 §3].
- A new offence in section 3(2B) covers collecting or providing funds, property, assets, material support or resources for terrorist purposes, including travel to become a "foreign terrorist fighter" [029/2026 §4].
- The penalty is changed to imprisonment "or with a fine not exceeding one hundred million rupees, or with both" [029/2026 §4]; "seven days" becomes "fourteen working days" in sections 4(3) and 4A(1) [029/2026 §5, §6].

Caveats: This is a Bill dated 2026-04-09; it also inserts new sections 4J and 4K on special investigation techniques and joint investigation teams [029/2026 §12], and many other consequential amendments are not listed here.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 029/2026 §1, 029/2026 §12, 029/2026 §3, 029/2026 §5

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The **Appropriation Bill** [639/2025] (Bill, 2025-09-26) is the 2025 bill covering the Government’s budget and borrowing for financial year 2026 [639/2025 §1; §2].

- It authorizes estimated expenditure of “rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand” for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026 [639/2025 §2(1)].
- It authorizes borrowing, with outstanding balance capped at “rupees three thousand eight hundred billion” during/end of FY2026 [639/2025 §2(1)(b)].
- It also states expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund at “rupees four thousand five hundred forty-five billion six hundred forty-three million five hundred thirty-two thousand” [639/2025 §2(4)].
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 639/2025 §1

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation) Bill** (Bill, 2026-07-27) — note its title is printed as "Economic and Rural **Recourses** Development Foundation" [055/2026 §1].

- It constitutes the Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal [055/2026 §2(1)].
- Its objects include developing "all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" and rural/estate community empowerment and human resource development [055/2026 §3(1)(a), (b), (h)].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [055/2026 §2(2)].
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 055/2026 §2

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum suspension is **one year** — the Council may “suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year” [054/2026 §24].

- This applies in lieu of disenrolling a member found guilty of professional misconduct [054/2026 §24].

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
Under the Protection of Occupants Bill the period is **"more than three months"** of undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation, prior to the events in sections 3, 4 or 5 [004/2026 §2].

- The person must also be "in lawful occupation" of the premises [004/2026 §2].
- Note the text's wording is "undisturbed and uninterrupted", not "peacefully" [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is the Bill version (2026-01-20); no GS version appears in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
Under the Gambling Regulatory Authority Bill (Bill, 2025-06-17), a person is disqualified from being **appointed** to the Board if he "is over seventy years of age" — i.e. 70 [613/2025 §9(i)].

- The disqualification sits in the list of grounds in §9, alongside being an MP, an undischarged bankrupt, or holding a gambling interest [613/2025 §9].
- Appointed members otherwise hold office "for a period of three years", with re-appointment for "not more than two further terms" [613/2025 §10].

Caveats: The text bars appointment of a person already over 70; no provision states that a sitting member must vacate the Board on reaching 70, and no other age limit for Board service appears in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The longest jail term is **one year**: the offence is punishable by a fine not exceeding three times the value of the cash/instruments **“or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year, or to both”** [021/2026 §31].

- This appears in the **Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment)** bill (GS, 2026-03-17), substituting section 27 of the principal Act [021/2026 §31].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version only; no presented Bill version is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
The bill sets a **late payment fee "equal to twice the annual subscription"**, payable by 30 April of the following year [072/2026 §30(4)].

- No fixed rupee amount is stated — the penalty is calculated as double the annual subscription, which itself is "as specified by rules" [072/2026 §30(1)].
- If the subscription plus late fee is still unpaid by that due date, the member "shall automatically forfeit its voting right" [072/2026 §30(5)]; after a further six months they are removed from the Register of Members [072/2026 §30(6)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (GS, 28.09.2026) of the "Sri Lanka Cricket Act" — no presented Bill version appears in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The Act does not set a payment date. [009/2026 §12] only fixes *which* debts carry over — those "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" — and says they "shall be paid by the body corporate hereby constituted," with no time limit stated.

- Cut-off date, not a deadline: liabilities of the Trust on the day before commencement pass to the body corporate [009/2026 §12].
- Same clause also assigns debts due to, and subscriptions/contributions payable to, the Trust on that day [009/2026 §12].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version (009/2026, GS 2026-02-05); a presented Bill version, which could differ, is not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the Immigration Bill (2026-10-07), the penalty is a fine of **not less than LKR 100,000 and not more than LKR 500,000** [082/2026 §90(2)].

- This applies to the vessel’s master, aircraft captain, or agent who fails to notify an Immigration Officer that a transit passenger or crew member did not continue their journey and appears to have remained in Sri Lanka [082/2026 §90(1)–(2)].
- The liability is “jointly and severally” on conviction; no imprisonment is specified for this offence [082/2026 §90(2)].

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
The Board Chairman serves a term of **three years** and is eligible for reappointment [636/2025 §11].

- The Minister appoints one appointed member as Chairman on the recommendation of the majority of ex-officio members [636/2025 §11].
- The text says: “shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for reappointment” [636/2025 §11].

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The new definition in section 52 states: "**Director-General**" means the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, "appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act" [595/2025 §6].

- The bill is the Rubber Control (Amendment), GS dated 2025-05-28 (Gazette version, not the presented Bill) [595/2025 §1].
- It also replaces "Controller"/"Rubber Controller" throughout the principal enactment with "Director-General" [595/2025 §2].

Caveats: Only the GS version is in evidence; no presented-Bill text or committee amendments.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 595/2025 §1, 595/2025 §6

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
The evidence I have is the Personal Data Protection Bill as published in the Gazette on 2021-11-25 (not an amendment Act), and it defines "public authority" broadly [152/2021 §47].

- Covers "a Ministry, any Department or Provincial Council, local authority, public corporation, statutory body or any institution established by any written law", including bodies established by a Provincial Council [152/2021 §47].
- Also includes "a company registered under the Companies Act, No. 7 of 2007 in which the government or a public corporation or a local authority directly holds fifty per centum or more of the shares" [152/2021 §47].

Caveats: No amended text is in the evidence; the question's "amended Act" appears to refer to this 2021 Gazette bill only.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
The amendment defines an “Export Agricultural Crop” as a crop with export potential in addition to local consumption, subject to exclusions and ministerial declaration [045/2026 §5].

- It must be “identified as a crop that have an export potential in addition to the local consumption” [045/2026 §5].
- It excludes “paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops” [045/2026 §5].
- The Minister must declare it “a notified agricultural crop” under section 2, and it “shall not include any crop identified as a plantation crop” [045/2026 §5].

Caveats: This is from the GS version dated 2026-06-25 of the Promotion of Export Agriculture (Amendment); no presented Bill version is in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka (Incorporation) Bill (GS, 2025-05-29), “qualified auditor” is defined in [597/2025 §10] as:

- An individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or another institute established by law and holds a “certificate to practice as an Accountant” from that Council; or
- A firm of accountants whose resident partners each meet that membership and certificate requirement.

Caveat: this evidence is the GS version, not a presented Bill.

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the **Proceeds of Crime** bill (GS version, 2025-02-21), an investigation officer may use five advanced techniques with a Magistrate’s authorization: “controlled delivery,” “digital surveillance” including interception/recording, “undercover operations including those involving the use of decoys,” “laying of traps,” and “forensic extraction” from digital devices [570/2025 §60(1)].

- Authorization is sought under section 56; the Magistrate may impose conditions [570/2025 §60(2)].
- The Magistrate must consider “necessity and justification” and proportionality [570/2025 §60(3)].
- The officer must report progress to the Magistrate “once in fourteen days” [570/2025 §60(4)].

Caveats: Evidence is the GS version only; no presented Bill or committee amendments are included.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
The quorum is **five members, “including the Chairperson”** [054/2026 §7(2)].

- The text does not expressly address whether the Chairperson’s presence can be dispensed with for quorum; it separately allows the Vice-Chairperson to preside if the Chairperson is absent [054/2026 §7(5)(b)].

Caveats: The bill’s quorum wording and absence-presiding rule are not expressly reconciled.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
The bill inserts a new section 38A requiring the Commission to compute fares by a formula it determines, publish the fare lists online, and requiring each operator to display a fare list in the vehicle [577/2025 §19].

- Formula is set "adhering to the national policy relating to transportation fares approved by Parliament, and specified by Order published in the Gazette"; the Commission also determines the formula after "written representations of the relevant stakeholders" and revises it periodically [577/2025 §19; 577/2025 §5].
- Providers must prepare their fare list per the website lists and display it "at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle"; the Commission may inspect compliance, and non-compliance is an offence under section 40 [577/2025 §19].
- Section 40 as amended: fine "not less than two hundred and fifty thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding five years" [577/2025 §23].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version of 2025-04-07; no presented Bill text is in the evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 577/2025 §23

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
The bill gives the “Mass Foundation” “perpetual succession” as a body corporate, with power to “sue and be sued” and to keep and alter a common seal [037/2026 §2]. It is deemed a “Voluntary Social Service Organization” under Act No. 31 of 1980 [037/2026 §2].

- Seal use requires two Committee members present to sign the instrument independently [037/2026 §15(1)].
- The seal is held in custody of a Committee office bearer chosen by the Committee [037/2026 §15(2)].
- The VSSO Act’s provisions apply to management of its affairs [037/2026 §2(2)].

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
Per the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (Amendment) Bill (Bill, 2026-07-21), new section 57a applies Part III to industrial-park transfers, and proviso (a) reads "the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government" as "the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka … or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution" as the case may be [053/2026 §10].

- Proviso (b) separately covers community based organizations: "the Minister assigned the subject of community based water supply under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution" [053/2026 §10].
- Section 16(d) similarly contemplates transfer by "voluntary transfer order or a compulsory transfer order under section 64" [053/2026 §2].

Caveats: the text does not say which of the two ministers applies to an industrial park specifically, and the substitution is garbled/truncated mid-clause; that detail is missing.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 053/2026 §2

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (Bill version, dated 2026-10-06), the Magistrate in whose jurisdiction an approved place of detention lies must visit it monthly and inspect it without advance notice [078/2026 §33(1)].

- Must visit "once a month", "without giving any advance notice", interview suspects, look into their well-being, and inspect "detention registers, Detention Orders and other books and documents" [078/2026 §33(1)].
- On suspect allegation or observation of torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, must "forthwith" order production for examination by a Judicial Medical Officer and receive the report [078/2026 §33(4)].
- If satisfied on reasonable grounds, must act under section 31 — e.g. direct medical treatment and change the place of detention [078/2026 §33(5), §31(1)].

Caveats: The first-produced Magistrate has similar visitation powers; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus [078/2026 §33(2)].

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill applies to "civil and commercial disputes" settled by mediation — whether under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [622/2025 §2(1)]; it does not list which substantive civil or commercial claims qualify beyond that general description.

- Excluded by statute: disputes required to be mediated under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003, which cannot be brought under this Act [622/2025 §2(2)–(3)].
- Excluded by subject matter: disputes needing terms enforceable "only on a decree or order of court", including the schedule items — divorce, nullity, persons of unsound mind/minors/wards, adoption, partition for rights in rem, probate, insolvency, admiralty in rem, fundamental-rights breaches [622/2025 §3; §30 schedule].
- Such excluded matters may still be mediated to produce terms of settlement for court [622/2025 §3 proviso].

Caveats: Evidence is incomplete — no passage affirmatively defines the scope of mediateable civil/commercial disputes beyond §2(1); the bill title is Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, dated 2025-07-11.

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the Samurdhi (Amendment) — Gazette version (GS), 2025-06-04 — new section 35A applies Article 154 of the Constitution (audit of public corporations' accounts) and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 to the audit of samurdhi community based banking societies' accounts [600/2025 §3].

- New section 28A makes the same audit provisions apply to samurdhi community based banks [600/2025 §2].
- In any Sinhala/Tamil inconsistency, the Sinhala text prevails [600/2025 §4].

Caveats: Only the GS version is in evidence; no presented Bill version or commencement/effective-date clause is shown.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The remedy is in the Companies (Amendment) bill, GS 2025-04-24 [582/2025 §17]: a company struck off under subsection (3) may apply to court, with the Attorney-General made a party, to be permitted re-registration.

- The application must be made "before the expiry of a period of ten years from the date of operation" of the Act; the court may permit re-registration and "make an order for the return to the company of all property previously vested in the State" [582/2025 §17].
- Property previously vested in the State: third parties who acquired rights from the State in good faith are unaffected, and where property is destroyed/damaged or possession not taken, the State is not liable [582/2025 §17].

Caveats: the text does not set out the grounds or procedure for the original striking off under section 487(3), only this proviso.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
The evidence only shows one bail provision: clause 17 of the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) bill (GS, 27 July 2026), which replaces section 149(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act No. 9 of 2023. Under it, all offences are "cognizable and non-bailable", with bail refused except in "exceptional circumstances by a High Court" where the thresholds below are met [051/2026 §17].

- Bribe of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees" solicited, accepted or offered [051/2026 §17].
- Loss caused to the Government of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees" [051/2026 §17].
- Benefit, favour or advantage to himself or another of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees" [051/2026 §17].

The value must be "confirmed by the Director-General by issuing a certificate" [051/2026 §17].

Caveats: no other bill in the evidence touches bail, and the 2023 Act's original section 149 text is not reproduced here, so I cannot confirm how far this differs from the existing law.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under the Gazette bill (GS, 30 Sep 2026) they are deemed **not** to be offences of a political character, or connected with/inspired by political motives, for extradition purposes with UN member states.

- §11 overrides the Extradition Law No. 8 of 1977: such offences "shall, for the purposes of that Law, be deemed not to be an offence of a political character…" — only "for the purposes only of extradition" as between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State, or assistance under section 12 [073/2026 §11].
- Related: §8 inserts an offence under this Act into the Schedule before Part B, and §9 deems existing extradition arrangements with UN member states to cover these offences [073/2026 §8][073/2026 §9].

Caveats: this is the Gazette version only; no presented Bill text is in evidence.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the amended section 23r, conviction before the Magistrate carries a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus a continuing-offence fine of "five thousand rupees for each day" after conviction [032/2026 §18].

- The original lower range ("not less than rupees ten thousand and not exceeding rupees one hundred thousand") and daily "rupees five hundred" are replaced [032/2026 §18].

Caveats: This is the National Environmental (Amendment) Bill (2026-05-06); the corpus contains only this presented Bill, not a Gazette version.

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment replaces the graduated fine in section 42 of the National Audit Act with "a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both" [611/2025 §13].

- The offence's old penalty (fine "not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees") is expressly substituted [611/2025 §13].
- This is from the Gazette version of the National Audit (Amendment) bill, dated 2025-06-23 [611/2025 §13].

Caveats: The evidence does not reproduce section 42 itself, so the conduct constituting the offence is not stated here.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
A penalty of **two thousand rupees**, in addition to the section 5 registration fee, applies; the local authority must also “take steps to vaccinate and register such dog immediately” in the Register of Dogs [066/2026 §7(4)].

- The notice gives **fourteen days**, extendable by a further fourteen days for a reasonable cause [066/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- This is from the **GS** version dated 2026-09-07, titled *Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs* [066/2026 §7].

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The bill adds "methamphetamine" to the named-drug lists in sections 54A and 54AA, and creates a new offence for manufacturing the other Third Schedule drugs (Groups A–E).

- §2 inserts "methamphetamine" into s.54A(1)(a) and adds paragraph (aa): manufacturing any other Group A–E drug is an offence triable by the High Court "without a jury" [068/2026 §2].
- Penalty for that new offence: fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or imprisonment "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both [068/2026 §2].
- §3 makes the same methamphetamine addition to s.54AA(1) [068/2026 §3].

Caveats: Figures are quoted from the Bill text (2026-09-08); no presented-Bill or later version appears in the evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 068/2026 §3

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. On and after the date of commencement, those benefits "shall no longer be provided with or paid to" former Presidents or their widows [627/2025 §3].

- Residence and monthly allowance for a former President or a former President's widow cease [627/2025 §3(a)].
- Monthly secretarial allowance, official transport and "such other facilities" cease [627/2025 §3(b)].
- The widow's monthly pension ceases [627/2025 §3(c)]; this follows the repeal of the 1986 Act [627/2025 §2].

Caveats: Bill dated 2025-08-07; no separate commencement date is given in the evidence, and committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
Under the proposed Penal Code amendment, causing **grievous hurt** to a person under 18 is punishable with imprisonment “of either description” for up to **ten years**, and the offender “shall also be liable to fine”; compensation may also be ordered. [618/2025 §6]

- The offence is new section **316a**, except in the case provided by section 326. [618/2025 §6]
- Compensation is determined after a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses. [618/2025 §6]

Caveats: This is the **Penal Code (Amendment) - GS** version dated 2025-07-08; “serious injury” is rendered as “grievous hurt” in the text.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The Gazette bill [017/2026] amends Section 5(1): paragraph (c) is cut off at "prior to April 1, 2026", and a new paragraph (d) applies to periods "commencing on or after April 1, 2026" with a four-quarter turnover ceiling of "thirty-six million rupees". [017/2026 §3]

- The existing (c) words "sixty million rupees." become "sixty million rupees; or" and its date range ends 1 April 2026. [017/2026 §3(2)]
- Paragraph (b)'s "hundred and twenty million rupees" only loses its "or" — the figure itself is unchanged. [017/2026 §3(1)]
- This version is the GS published 2026-03-03, not a presented Bill. [017/2026 §3]

Caveats: §3's wording is garbled, and the evidence does not spell out the full turnover-threshold structure of Section 5 or how the new 36 million rupee limit interacts with the other paragraphs.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment to Section 14 raises the ownership threshold from “more than fifty per centum” to “one hundred per centum” and shifts the covered entities from “person” to a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007 [584/2025 §12].

- Ownership: replaces “more than fifty per centum” with “one hundred per centum” [584/2025 §12(1)].
- Entity in subsection (2): replaces “Any person who” with “Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which” [584/2025 §12(2)].
- Entity in subsection (3): replaces “a person who” with “a company, which” [584/2025 §12(3)].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The bill amends section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance by repealing paragraph (n) and by rewording the definition of "express trust" in paragraph (p). [081/2026 §2]

- Paragraph "(n)" of section 3 is repealed outright; the bill does not say what that paragraph contained. [081/2026 §2]
- In paragraph (p), the words "trust generally in the form" in the definition of "express trust" are replaced by "trust in the form". [081/2026 §2]

Caveats: This is the Trusts (Amendment) — GS (Gazette, 14 Oct 2026); no presented-Bill version appears in the evidence, and the effect of the change is not explained in the text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The bill raises the age in section 6(3) of the Judicature Act from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years", and replaces section 6(4) so that the retirement age of "all other Judges and Magistrates" is "sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3].

- New s.6(4) applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [058/2026 §3].
- This is the Gazette version (GS, 2026-08-07) of the Judicature (Amendment) [058/2026 §1].

Caveats: the text quoted does not identify which judges fall under s.6(3); no presented Bill version is in evidence.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 058/2026 §1

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer: A person may not be appointed Dean of a Faculty for **more than two terms**, under the new subsection (4) inserted into section 49 [649/2025 §2]. This is from the Universities (Amendment) **GS** dated 2025-11-21.

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:

- It provides that debts and liabilities of the existing Institute pass to the "body corporate hereby constituted" on commencement [628/2025 §3].

Caveats: The short-title/incorporation clause itself is not among the passages, so the name is taken from the Bill's title; "IFMSL" is defined as the existing professional body [628/2025 §3]. Not legal advice.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
